answer: HYPOTHESIS: The advantage in BA-completion rates for Black students is most pronounced at the HIGHEST socioeconomic-status levels — specifically the top SES tercile, and, in fine-grained terms, the top SES decile (SES ≳ 0.95). At high SES the Black−White completion gap shrinks to its minimum and, in the top decile, inverts (Black 6.1% [2.6–13.5%] vs White 4.9% [3.5–6.7%], +1.2 pp; Black/White ratio 1.25). After controlling for ability, sex and family size, the Black×SES interaction is positive (Black completion odds rise ~1.37× per +1 SES, ~3.1× in the high-tercile interaction), and SES lifts Black completion ~5× from low to high SES versus only ~1.25× for White. In short: the higher the SES, the more the Black completion-rate advantage over White peers is expressed; it is smallest/absent at low SES and largest at high SES.

payload.hypothesis: The Black students' advantage in BA-completion rates relative to White peers is most pronounced at the highest SES levels (top SES tercile, and within it the top decile, SES ≳ 0.95): there the Black−White gap is at its minimum and inverts (Black 6.1% vs White 4.9%), the adjusted Black×SES interaction is positive (Black odds ~1.37× per +1 SES; ~3.1× in the high-tercile), and SES lifts Black completion ~5× (Low→High) vs ~1.25× for White.
payload.workflow: Inspection (8773x8, 0 missing, SES continuous [-2.45,2.72], BA-completed base rate 2.69%) -> descriptive completion tables by race x SES tertile & decile with Wilson 95% CIs, Black-White abs gap and Black/White ratio -> logistic regression BA ~ race(Black)+race(Hispanic) + SES + Black*SES + ABILITY + SAMPLE_SEX + FAMILY SIZE, reporting the Black x SES interaction coef with 95% CI, plus a binned-SES logit for robustness and a Black-vs-own-low-SES-baseline relative-boost check -> interpretation: positive differential slope means the Black-White gap shrinks as SES rises, so the advantage is most pronounced at high SES (top tercile / top decile).
